svg.title: Dizziness: first decide whether it is true vertigo; non-vestibular dizziness has organic and psychiatric causes, while peripheral vertigo is named by how long attacks last and whether hearing is affected: BPPV, Meniere's disease, vestibular neuronitis or labyrinthitis, superior canal dehiscence, and aminoglycoside toxicity; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

svg.text: seconds: BPPV, dehiscence · minutes to hours: Ménière's (hearing lost) or migrainous (hearing kept) · days: labyrinthitis (hearing lost) or neuronitis (kept) · forever:
